note: _prolixior atque conscius clangor –_ a longer and uninterrupted tone; _pari ululatu tubae –_ the same howling of the trumpet_._ – Matthew A. Kraus: Auffallende Stellen zu Hörnern. In: Schmid/Fieger, pp. 51–53: the rendering in the German Tusculum-Vulgata is not exact. Num 13:30 (Vg 13:31). _murmur populi qui oriebatur contra Mosen_ (Benedictine Vulgate, Weber/Gryson, Clementina, NVg) – the murmuring of the people that arose against Moses. One would expect _quod_ (not _qui_), because _murmur_ is a neuter word. Friedrich Stummer (_Theologische Revue_ 36 [1937] 308) calls it a vulgarism. But it may be that the qui is linked to _populus_ (rather than to _murmur_).
